shots.text: The throne hall was in ruins. He was on his knees, and the thing he had become was cracking open.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The throne hall in ruins. Vael-Orrun on his knees; the monster shape cracks, and there is a tired man inside it.

shots.text: I gave away my forgetting, so I remember everything. You should know what we did.
shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: The six Wardens standing round him.

shots.text: He kept the peace between us for forty years. We feared him, and we wanted his gold.
shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: A painted memory: the Feast of the Crossroads. A kind king in grey, his wife and small son, six crowned guests, all smiling.

shots.text:
They came to his feast as friends. At midnight they opened his gates. His city burned, and his wife and son burned with it.

The songs call it a victory. The Wardens call it the Night of Six Knives.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The painting burns from the middle out.

shots.speaker: ignar
shots.art_note: Ignar, looking at his own hands.

shots.text: You did this. Remember that you did this.
shots.speaker: vael_orrun
shots.art_note: Vael-Orrun, quiet, not angry any more.

shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: Thalassa, bells silent in her hair.

shots.text:
It was never my voice in the dark. It spoke to me too.

It is still listening.
shots.speaker: vael_orrun
shots.art_note: The grey goes out of his eyes. He looks past the Wardens, past the heroes, at something behind the camera.

shots.text: Mirelle had seen a death at the end of the war. It was his.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Mirelle at the edge of the hall, blind eyes glowing teal.

shots.text:
Oswin set his lantern in the wound in his brow, where his crown once sat. He wanted the middle of the world. So we gave it to him.

Not as its king. As its light.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Oswin setting the white lantern into the crown-shaped wound. Vael-Orrun turns to light, and the light rises home toward Solenne, to the Heartstone that was his crown.
